topic: UNESCO World Heritage Sites and Intangible Heritage
description: This topic covers the Cultural, Natural, and Intangible heritages in India recognized by UNESCO. It is a highly crucial Static GK topic for competitive exams, requiring memorization of site locations, addition years, and unique features.

sections.title: Introduction to UNESCO and World Heritage
sections.description: Fundamental concepts regarding UNESCO and the current status of World Heritage Sites in India.

key_concepts.concept: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)
key_concepts.explanation: A specialized agency of the UN headquartered in Paris, France, aimed at promoting world peace and security through international cooperation in education, arts, sciences, and culture.
Landmarks or areas with legal protection by an international convention administered by UNESCO, designated for having Outstanding Universal Value to humanity.

important_facts.fact: India currently has a total of 42 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, which include 34 Cultural, 7 Natural, and 1 Mixed site.
World Heritage Day (International Day for Monuments and Sites) is observed globally on April 18 every year.
The World Heritage Committee meets annually to decide which newly nominated sites will be added to the official list.

sections.title: Major Cultural Heritage Sites of India
sections.description: Prominent cultural sites representing India's historical and architectural brilliance.

historical_events.significance: Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and the Taj Mahal were the first four sites from India to be inscribed on the UNESCO list.

key_associations.extra_info: Built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I, it is also famously known as the 'Black Pagoda'.
The erstwhile capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
Built by the Chandela Dynasty, famous for its Nagara style architecture and erotic sculptures.
A highly revered Buddhist pilgrimage site where Lord Buddha attained Enlightenment.

sections.title: Natural and Mixed Heritage Sites of India
sections.description: Crucial ecosystems recognized for their outstanding biodiversity and natural beauty.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Home to two-thirds of the world's population of the Great One-horned Rhinoceros. (Inscribed: 1985)
The largest mangrove forest in the world and the core habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger. (Inscribed: 1987)

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala
geographical_data.key_characteristics: A massive mountain range running parallel to the western coast, recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot. (Inscribed: 2012)
India's only 'Mixed' World Heritage Site, valued for both its stunning natural landscape and cultural significance. (Inscribed: 2016)

sections.title: Recently Added World Heritage Sites
sections.description: Newly inducted UNESCO sites in India, highly relevant for Current Affairs and latest Static GK.

historical_events.event: Inclusion of Dholavira and Ramappa Temple
historical_events.significance: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple in Telangana became the 39th site, and Dholavira (a Harappan city in Gujarat) became India's 40th site.

historical_events.event: Inclusion of Santiniketan and Hoysala Temples
historical_events.significance: Santiniketan in West Bengal (established by Rabindranath Tagore) became the 41st site, and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas in Karnataka became the 42nd site.

sections.title: Intangible Cultural Heritage of India
sections.description: Traditions, performing arts, and festivals of India recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH).

key_concepts.explanation: Practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, and skills transmitted from generation to generation. India currently has 15 items on this prestigious UNESCO list.

key_associations.extra_info: The 15th and latest Intangible Cultural Heritage from India, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023.
A major Hindu festival celebrating the goddess Durga, added to the ICH list in December 2021.
The world's largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims, recognized by UNESCO in 2017.
A famous folk dance performed by the snake charmer community of Rajasthan, inscribed in 2010.
A traditional dance form with strong martial arts roots and folk traditions, inscribed in 2010.
